officialDocs.label: How to publish an app (partner requirements)

verdict.summary: OAuth is only available to accepted Aircall Technology Partners. To be accepted you need a live product and an active customer base; Aircall then creates your dev and prod OAuth apps, reviews a demo before publishing, and lists you on the public Marketplace only after 10 customers. Once installed by a customer admin, the token is company-wide and never expires.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Partner application answered within 5 business days, then an integration plan, then Aircall creates the trial developer account and OAuth apps; only the 5-day figure is published.

timeToProd.assumes: A Public App installable by any Aircall customer from the Dashboard (published after demo review); the public Marketplace listing comes later, at 10 customers.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Technology Partner acceptance (up to 5 business days), Aircall creating credentials, demo/asset review (1–5 business days) and publishing (3–5 business days), plus your own build time.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Review windows are sourced; the total includes estimated build time and the unpublished credential turnaround.

prerequisites.item: A live, established product with a company website and an active customer base
prerequisites.why: These are the stated requirements for Technology Partner acceptance, which OAuth depends on; meeting them doesn't guarantee approval.

prerequisites.item: Public HTTPS install URI and redirect URI(s) (no localhost)
prerequisites.why: Prod apps need an installation URI; both dev and prod accept up to five redirect URIs, and localhost isn't supported.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Use a tunnel such as ngrok during development.

prerequisites.item: Demo video (5–10 min), two help-center articles, SVG logo and 3–5 screenshots
prerequisites.why: Required review assets before Aircall publishes the app.

scopeTiers.impact: The only documented scope. Gives a company-scoped token for calls, users, contacts, numbers and webhooks once a customer admin installs the app.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Time is inferred from the launch process.

examples: Conversation Intelligence trackers (AI Assist / AI Assist Pro)
scopeTiers.impact: Transcripts/AI and analytics data an agent may want only work for customers with the matching paid package.

scopeTiers.tier: Private app (API key, your own account only)
scopeTiers.impact: Any Aircall customer can create API keys for their own company, but this can't be distributed to other customers.

steps.title: Check partner eligibility
steps.detail: Confirm you have a live product, public website and active customers, and draft the partner application.

steps.title: Apply to the Technology Partner program

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Signup URL returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-20; we didn't submit it.

steps.title: Wait for partner decision
steps.detail: Aircall says it gets back within 5 business days and may decline at its discretion.

steps.title: Send the integration plan
steps.detail: Draft a short plan (goals, what you'll build, main features) plus install URI and redirect URIs for dev and prod. Unanswered applications are discarded after a month.

steps.title: Receive developer account and OAuth apps
steps.detail: Aircall creates a 4-month trial developer account and separate dev and prod OAuth apps (client ID and secret).

steps.title: Implement the install + OAuth flow
steps.detail: Handle the GET to your install_uri, redirect to https://dashboard.aircall.io/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, scope=public_api and state; exchange the code (valid 10 min, single use) via JSON POST to https://api.aircall.io/v1/oauth/token; verify with GET /v1/ping.

steps.title: Build rate-limit and uninstall handling
steps.detail: Respect 120 requests/min per company using X-AircallApi-Remaining/Reset, and handle uninstall/reinstall (a reinstall issues a new token).

steps.title: Send progress updates during the build
steps.detail: Aircall expects completion within 6 months and an update at least every 2 months, otherwise assets are decommissioned.

steps.title: Record the demo and prepare listing assets
steps.detail: Record a 5–10 minute demo; prepare the SVG logo from the Figma template and screenshots. An agent can draft the two help-center articles.

steps.title: Demo and asset review
steps.detail: Aircall reviews the demo and assets.

steps.title: Publication in the Aircall Dashboard
steps.detail: Aircall publishes the app in the Dashboard (not yet the public Marketplace); customer admins can now install it.

steps.title: Request Marketplace listing at 10 customers
steps.detail: Email Aircall once 10 customers use the app to get listed on the public Marketplace; the trial dev account is then extended indefinitely.

agentCanDo: Draft the partner application and integration plan
Implement the install_uri handler, OAuth code exchange and /v1/ping check
Build 120 req/min per-company rate limiting and reinstall handling
Draft the two help-center articles and listing copy
humanMustDo: Apply to the Technology Partner program and respond to Aircall
Store the client secrets Aircall provides
Send progress updates at least every two months
Record the demo video and submit assets
Customer side: an Aircall Admin installs the app

blockers.symptom: No way to create OAuth credentials in the Aircall dashboard
blockers.cause: OAuth is only for accepted Technology Partners; customers only get API keys.
blockers.fix: Apply to the partner program, or use an API key for a single-company private app.

blockers.cause: No live product, website or active customer base, or Aircall's discretion.
blockers.fix: Reapply once you have paying customers and a public product.

blockers.symptom: Non-admin users are redirected away from the consent screen
blockers.cause: Only Aircall Admin users can approve and install integrations.
blockers.fix: Ask the customer's Aircall admin to install the app.
Use an HTTPS tunnel such as ngrok and register that URL.

blockers.symptom: Token exchange returns {"message":"BadRequestException","details":"Missing code field in body"}
blockers.cause: The JSON body is missing code (or the code expired after 10 minutes).
blockers.fix: Send code, redirect_uri, client_id, client_secret and grant_type as JSON immediately after the callback.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Observed with an empty JSON POST on 2026-10-20.

blockers.symptom: Developer account or OAuth apps disabled mid-build
blockers.cause: No progress update for over two months; Aircall decommissions assets after follow-ups.
blockers.fix: Send updates at least every two months.

nuances.text: OAuth access tokens don't expire and have no refresh flow; a token is scoped to one Aircall company and replaced only on reinstall, so store it like a long-lived secret.
Rate limit is 120 requests/minute per company, shared across all keys and tokens for that company; increases go through support.
After publication the app shows in the Aircall Dashboard but not the public Marketplace until you reach 10 customers.
The developer account is a 4-month trial, extendable while you're in the program and made permanent after your first customers.
AI data such as Conversation Intelligence trackers needs the customer to have AI Assist or AI Assist Pro, so an agent's features may vary per customer.
